html:
SMTO-WEB-0057 — SMTO's follow-up question offered an option it hadn't found

GUID: 96c9a2f5-d6c9-5f9d-9336-583d81ee3040
Slug: research-clarification-candidate-unobserved
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • SMTO tried to ask which item you meant, but one of the choices it listed came from neither your message nor its research. That question was stopped before it reached you, and no new web searches were made.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment for SMTO to ask its question again. It will usually rephrase it using only options it actually found, or ask you openly. SMTO stops a question that suggests made-up options and asks again without them.
  2. If the run stops instead, type a new message in the conversation with the exact name, model number or a link to the item you mean. Giving the exact item yourself removes the need for SMTO to suggest options at all.
  3. When you reply to a list of options, choose only one you recognise as correct. If none fit, say none of them and describe the item. Picking a suggested option you don't recognise could send the research toward the wrong item.

What success looks like

  • SMTO asks which item you meant using only options from your message or its research, or carries on once you name the item.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't pick an option you don't recognise just to move on.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The web research clarification hook rejected an ask_user question because it proposes a literal identifier that appears neither in the observed alternatives nor in the user's own input.

What this means

  • A clarification question proposes a literal identifier absent from observed alternatives and the original user input. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • A clarification question proposes a literal identifier absent from observed alternatives and the original user input.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare identifiers in the question with observed_alternatives and original literal text.

How to fix it

  • In requested (skills/web_research/entities.py) every literal span in the ask_user question must match a user input or an identifier in entity_resolutions[*].observed_alternatives. Rewrite the question to offer only those identifiers, or ask an open question; the rejection performs no new retrieval and does not establish the content of unread sources.
  • Offer only identifiers present in observed_alternatives or user input, or ask an open question.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The clarification uses observed choices or an open question without invented identifiers.

What not to do

  • Do not offer an invented identifier as an observed clarification candidate.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
